items.topic: Create signup first, then match player
items.statement: Kobi described the flow: create a signup record on every inbound API call whether or not a player exists, then a flow matches by email to an existing player or creates one, so API calls are never blocked.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: That means we are going to create a signup record anytime an API call is made out from your back end to create a signup record whether there's a player or not. But the moment that's created, then we we have a flow that tries to match that sign up with the email address to an existing player. / Kobi Kunasekaran: And if one doesn't exist, then create that player and then associate that sign up with the player.

items.topic: Re-clicks must not be dropped as duplicates
items.statement: Today a player's repeat click on the same operator link is treated as a duplicate and not registered. Joyce wants repeat clicks reflected because conversion timing is unknown; Kobi agreed.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: week. Um, and we have no way of tracking our system today on if they clicked that affiliate link again because the system is treating that as a ddupe or as a duplicate. / Kobi Kunasekaran: would you want two signup records reflected in Salesforce or a single one? / Joyce Kiddell: I would say both just because we don't know when the player is going to end up actually / Kobi Kunasekaran: Yeah, I agree with you.

items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: prioritize in view of the rep so that they know that it was clicked again but it doesn't necessarily have to create two / Joyce Kiddell: separate items or rows if you follow what I'm saying then I think that's probably the preferred method so we don't have to like stiff through a bunch of duplicate entries and archive them. / Joyce Kiddell: Yeah. Yeah. Like if we can have a concept in one sign of record for that individual player and then like a an audit trail

items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: under the bucket of like didn't convert? So like I'm even though it did, right? But like just later on. items.quote: Waleed Alasadi: given your model, given the API, I think we can achieve the same thing with like a contact life cycle status versus a lead life cycle status. / Joyce Kiddell: super aligned bully and I think that's what I was hinting at in the PRD in terms of like converting from like a lead to a a signup and that it's more of a status thing versus like me / Kobi Kunasekaran: That's better.

items.topic: Current state: study link click creates Lead
items.statement: Kobi described his understanding of the current state: a study link click creates a Lead record in Salesforce, and a survey completion updates the lead with a survey-completed checkbox. Calls to Salesforce come from the WagerTech back end. The client did not correct this.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: And when they click on those study links, that's when a lead record is created in Salesforce today. Um, and I believe there's also uh there are survey links on the agency websites as well. when they complete a survey, then those lead records get updated and the ser it there's a checkbox that it says survey has been completed.
items.critic_note: Kobi's stated understanding of the current system ("I believe"); not explicitly confirmed by the client, so firmness discussed.

items.feature_area: Other (external operator data store / Postgres integration)
items.topic: Kobi to find SF-to-Postgres loader name
items.statement: Kobi said he will find the name of a low-cost tool he used before to load Salesforce data into Postgres. (Cost detail and other-engagement reference on the same line withheld under rule 5.)
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: I can't remember the name of it but I will find it for you

items.feature_area: Other (data model alignment with client ERD)
items.topic: How ERD deviations get communicated
items.statement: Strahinja said Jumpr does not need to edit his ERD; if a change is coming, Jumpr can point him to the Salesforce diagram and he will update the ERD. Kobi answered that his user stories (field, API and display names) are a good way to review changes. No single mechanism was confirmed.
items.quote: Strahinja Vladetic: So if anything if you guys know that there's a change coming um you guys can just point me to the diagram and I can make the updates. / Kobi Kunasekaran: Okay. Like next steps for for my end is to write up the user stories for like the objects that we need to create or update.

items.topic: Salesforce naming will differ from ERD
items.statement: Kobi said Salesforce naming conventions (custom field suffix, separate API name and label) mean names cannot match the ERD exactly, and Salesforce will likely end up with many more fields (reporting, formula, display) than the ERD. He left it to Strahinja whether to bring all fields into the ERD. This partly limits the naming-consistency request in item -20.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: Um and then like Salesforce has specific naming conventions as well. So we won't be able to do it exactly like this. / Kobi Kunasekaran: So, we're going to likely have a lot more than what's here or what's defined um by the end of this project.

items.topic: Existing build lacks design rationale
items.statement: Emily said the existing build was not meant to work through the bigger model design questions, and WagerTech may not have a sound reason for many existing decisions that Jumpr will question. Joyce said the Lead setup came from the previous developer.
items.quote: Emily Vandenberg: I'm sure there's going to be many instances where you're questioning the why and I don't think we have like a sound reason / Joyce Kiddell: Um, but I think that's how we did have it set up from the previous developer.

items.topic: Client feedback on current build not covered
items.statement: Kobi noted the plan to walk through the Salesforce build and get the client's feedback on what they liked and did not like. The meeting ran out of time after the signup discussion; the transcript shows no such walkthrough in this meeting.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: we want to go through the Salesforce uh Salesforce build as well and like you were going to provide uh like your feedback on things that you liked um and things that you didn't like.

items.topic: Test name matching with data analysis
items.statement: Waleed suggested that, if WagerTech really wants name matching, Jumpr could run the client data set through an AI analysis to see how often name matching would have worked. No one took this up.
items.quote: Waleed Alasadi: I I mean what I was going to suggest if we do like just really want to use name that we pass your data set through like AI analysis to see how many times they would have caught name versus like didn't.

items.topic: Reduce proof storage cost to minimum
items.statement: Joyce said WagerTech wants to bring its current proof-storage (Dropbox) cost down as far as possible and asked Jumpr for a specific recommendation based on actual usage. (Figures withheld under rule 5.)
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: So, we know we want to get that down. um to like nothing if possible.

items.topic: Joyce sent Dropbox usage and licenses
items.statement: During the meeting Joyce sent Kobi the exact Dropbox usage amount and the number of licenses.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: Yeah. Okay. I just sent you the exact amount um and how many licenses and stuff we have.

notes: Read all lines. First ~33 min: data architecture with Strahinja (Postgres for operator data, reporting joins). Then weekly sync: status, signup model (Lead replaced by signup record; duplicate click handling pending Kobi's document; email-first matching with rep review queue), storage (Dropbox vs Salesforce native vs GCP). Meeting time 12:00 from file name; transcript says the meeting was moved to 12:30. No Jira keys spoken. Rule 5: skipped Salesforce partner/list pricing and promo discussion (~L927-941), storage/Dropbox cost figures (~L905-907, L952, L1012), and a middleware tool cost that also referenced another engagement (~L460). Waleed slipped and named another client at L192; that part is left out of quotes. Gemini 'Aligned' decisions on signup records, secondary email and review queue are supported by transcript; GCP 'selected' is over-firm.
critic_notes: Critic read all 1033 lines. All 56 original quotes found at stated lines (some quotes put a speaker prefix on a mid-line fragment). Added 10 items (-57 to -66). Modified 3 (-24, -44, -46). Added 2 Gemini disagreements. No secrets seen. Rule 5 respected: no figures or other-client names quoted in new items.
